title: Route two_device_sync_test.dart's S1/S3 through the real MergeRouter instead of hand-decoding outbox JSON

evidence.quote: final data = jsonDecode(row.payload) as Map<String, dynamic>;

why: test/sync/two_device_sync_test.dart and test/integration/two_device_sync_test.dart share the exact same name and the same group label ('I-5: two-device sync scenarios' / 'Two-device convergence test harness (I-5)'), created about an hour apart on the same day. The integration version carries @Tags(['i5','two_device_sync']) and drives the real MergeRouter/CompletionEventMerger/EntityMerger stack — it is the file docs/sync-conflict-resolution.md names as the canonical I-5 harness (completion set-union, track-deactivation LWW, idempotent re-merge). The file in this batch has no tags at all and, for S1 ('completion propagates to Device B'), never imports MergeRouter/EntityMerger — it hand-decodes the outbox JSON payload and calls completionEventDao.appendEvent directly, bypassing every line of the actual merge/dispatch code Device B's real pull uses. A regression in CompletionEventMerger's field mapping or LWW comparison would not be caught here; a reader trusting the group name would believe cross-device merge logic is under test when it isn't, and it also doesn't cover track-deactivation LWW at all (only the integration twin does).
recommendation: Either delete test/sync/two_device_sync_test.dart's S1/S3 in favor of the tag-carrying, merge-router-driven test/integration/two_device_sync_test.dart (keeping S2's soft-delete-outbox scenario, relocated since it's not duplicated there), or rewrite S1's simulated pull to dispatch through the real MergeRouter/CompletionEventMerger so the test exercises production code and add the i5/two_device_sync tags for consistency.
acceptance_criteria: Only one file covers I-5 two-device completion propagation end-to-end through MergeRouter/CompletionEventMerger, or the two files are clearly differentiated in name and purpose.
Any surviving two_device_sync_test.dart file carries @Tags(['i5','two_device_sync']) matching its sibling.
